slides.text:
Many functions finish with a task that must always happen: closing something, releasing it, saying goodbye. `defer` lets you write that task right next to the code that needs it, and Go runs it when the function ends.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
work():
    open something
    run later: close it
    do the job
    (close runs here, on exit)

slides.text:
Two sessions:

- **Session 1:** what `defer` does, in what order and on an early return
- **Session 2:** when its values are read, closures and results
Put `defer` before a function call. The call does not run there: it waits until the surrounding function is about to return, and then it runs.
A function can defer many calls. They pile up like plates: the **last** one deferred is the **first** one to run.
Deferred calls run however the function ends: at its last line or at a `return` in the middle. That is why cleanup goes in a `defer` and not at the bottom, where an early `return` would skip it.

chunks.text:
func main() {
    fmt.Println("start")
    defer fmt.Println("one")
    defer fmt.Println("two")
    defer fmt.Println("three")
    fmt.Println("end")
}

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.explanation: Nothing deferred runs until `main` ends, so the loop prints first. Then the deferred calls run last in, first out: `b`, then `a`.

slides.text: When Go reaches a `defer`, it reads the **arguments** of the call at once and keeps them. Only the call itself waits. A change to the variable afterwards does not reach the deferred call.
slides.code:
x := 1
defer fmt.Println(x)
x = 9    // the call keeps 1

slides.text: To see the latest value, defer a function literal that calls itself at the end. Its body runs late and, as a closure, reads the variable as it is **then**. The `()` after the literal is the call that `defer` needs.

A deferred closure runs after the `return` has set the result, and before the caller gets it. If the function has a **named result**, the closure can change it, and the caller receives the changed value.
